headline: Funding flows. Acquisitions happen. Tests delay.
deck: This week saw a mix of funding successes and notable acquisitions, while tests continued to slip.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amidst co-orbital hype
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding underscores the growing defense focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. As the DoD seeks innovative solutions, True Anomaly seems poised to capitalize on this trend.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that co-orbital security will be the next big thing, but let’s hope they aren’t just throwing darts at a board.

stories.head: Voyager snags Astrobotic for lunar ambitions
stories.body: Voyager Technologies has acquired Astrobotic Technology, just as the latter gears up for NASA's lunar lander missions. The deal positions Voyager to tap into the burgeoning lunar economy, which is expected to be worth billions. This acquisition comes at a time when lunar activities are ramping up significantly.
stories.soWhat: Acquiring a lunar lander company is like buying beachfront property before the ocean rises—timing is everything.

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests face another delay
stories.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has been delayed for the third consecutive quarter, raising questions about the program's viability. This marks a troubling trend for a technology that is supposed to be at the forefront of national defense. Delays like this could have implications for both funding and strategic planning.
stories.soWhat: If hypersonic tests keep slipping, we might need to redefine 'rapid prototyping' to mean 'whenever we get around to it.'

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on lunar developments
watchlist.body: With NASA's plans for a moon base and increasing private investments, the lunar landscape is changing rapidly.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-design review
watchlist.body: Now that the Dream Chaser DoD variant has passed its design review, the pressure is on for a timely launch.

watchlist.title: Palantir's government contracts expansion
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension on its TITAN program, Palantir is deepening its ties with the DoD.

watchlist.title: China's Long March 10C as a commercial player
watchlist.body: China's new rocket could reshape commercial launch dynamics, particularly as it gains traction in the global market.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.

Voyager's acquisition of Astrobotic positions it well for upcoming lunar missions.
